notice: Source-reviewed against Canadian government publications on 2026-10-26. Passenger and document data are fictional; no independent human review is claimed.

rules.title: A travel document is not always a national passport
rules.body: A boarding identity document must be genuine, current and accepted by Canada. IRCC accepts U.S. refugee travel documents (I-571) and re-entry permits (I-327). Issuance by the United States does not make the holder a U.S. citizen. Inspect the document category as well as the issuing country. Air Beluga fictional training procedure: resolve material identity or permission conflicts using the offered checks, then refer unresolved conflicts to a supervisor. This escalation procedure is a game rule, not an IRCC requirement.

rules.title: Canadian visitor permission is separate from a U.S. visa
rules.body: For these Indian and mainland Chinese visitors, a U.S. visitor or work visa does not replace Canadian visitor permission. Check for a Canadian visa or a separately applicable exemption, such as proven U.S. lawful permanent residence.

rules.title: U.S. permanent residents: identity plus status proof
rules.body: A U.S. lawful permanent resident travelling by air needs a valid national passport or accepted equivalent and current accepted proof of U.S. permanent-resident status. A valid Green Card is one such proof. These travellers do not need a Canadian visitor visa or eTA, including holders of Indian or Chinese passports.

rules.title: An expired card calls for supporting status evidence
rules.body: An expired Green Card by itself is not the current status proof listed by IRCC. Check for an accepted extension notice or another listed status document. Card expiry alone is not a determination that permanent-resident status has ended; the puzzle concerns whether sufficient boarding evidence has been presented.

rules.title: U.S. refugee document: visa or a proven exemption
rules.body: A U.S. I-571 refugee travel document is not proof of U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residence. The non-Canadian refugee-document holders in these cases need a Canadian visitor visa unless a separate exemption applies. An eTA is not the substitute for that visa.

rules.title: I-571 and I-327 have different evidence roles
rules.body: For the authored U.S. permanent residents unable to use a national passport, I-571 and I-327 are accepted identity substitutes. I-571 still needs separate permanent-resident proof. IRCC also lists a valid I-327 as accepted status proof, so the same valid I-327 can establish both roles in the authored case.

rules.title: Romania: check whether the passport is electronic
rules.body: Romania’s ordinary visa-exempt air-travel route is limited to electronic passport holders. A non-electronic temporary passport requires a Canadian visitor visa unless another applicable exemption is established. A past eTA email is not Canadian visa evidence.

rules.title: Diplomatic and official do not automatically mean visa-free
rules.body: In these Indian and Chinese visitor cases, diplomatic or official passport classification alone does not remove the Canadian visa requirement. A Canadian diplomatic accreditation or another applicable status exemption must be established separately. A fee exemption for official business is not a travel-permission exemption.
